subject: RE: Globex RFP — model catalog licensing, provenance attestation & pinning playbook
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@globex.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Globex Legal <legal@globex.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Globex RFP: model catalog licensing + provenance questions

Mina,

Thanks for taking our RFP. We have a short follow-up focused on model provenance, license compatibility, and expected update cadence for pinned models in your catalog. Please answer the items below as part of our supplier questionnaire so we can move to legal review: 

1) For open-models listed in your catalog, what license types do you surface (e.g., Apache 2.0, MIT, CC-BY, custom)? Please explain how you handle mixed-origin artifacts (weights licensed differently than code).

2) Do you provide a verifiable chain-of-custody / SBOM-like manifest for each catalog model? If so: format, signing, and retention period.

3) What is your recommended process for "pinning" a model version for production (how to request, how you guarantee immutability, rollback options, and time-to-delivery for backports)?

4) How do you communicate security or license changes that would require a customer action (e.g., license incompatibility, provenance revision)? Describe notification windows and automated policies if any.

5) Please attach a short attestation we can accept to include in our procurement file (we prefer a signed PDF).

We'd like answers by EOD Friday so legal can start redlines next week.

Thanks,
Alice Morton
Procurement Manager, Globex Corporation
procurement@globex.com

--
Globex RFP Coordinator
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@globex.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Globex RFP: model catalog licensing + provenance questions

Alice —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached are our initial responses (see 'Redwood_RFI_Answers_v1.pdf'). Below is a concise summary and proposed next steps so your legal team can triage quickly.

Summary answers (high level):
- License types: we enumerate license metadata per model in the catalog (common licenses: Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3, CC-BY-4.0). For mixed-origin artifacts we publish separate license fields for model weights, model code, tokenizer files, and evaluation artifacts; any restrictive component is flagged in the UI and manifest.
- Provenance / SBOM: we provide a machine-readable manifest (JSON-LD) and a human summary (PDF/CSV). Each manifest includes source commit hashes, upstream package refs, training data provenance tags (where available), and a generated material_signature (SHA256) for the packaged artifact. Artifacts are signed with our platform key; customers can request signed attestations on demand. Retention: manifests are retained for active catalog entries and historical snapshots for 36 months by default (extendable under contract).
- Pinning process: customers request a pin via Console (API + Console). We create an immutable snapshot (content-addressed storage) and return a pin token (model_id@hash). Immutability guarantee: snapshot is retained and tombstoned from automatic upgrades. Rollbacks: we support roll-forward and roll-back based on snapshot tokens; backport turnaround (for critical fixes) is SLA-driven for Dedicated/Private: <72 hours for security patches; Hosted: same-day mitigation + automatic compatible fallback while we process a pinned backport.
- Change notifications: license/provenance changes trigger a three-stage notification: 1) Informational (48 hours), 2) Action recommended (14 days), and 3) Required action (60 days for license-compatibility breaks). For critical security or license incompatibilities we provide immediate notifications plus automatic routing to compatible variants if available (configurable at the customer level).
- Attestation: we're happy to provide a signed attestation PDF — attached (initial draft). Please flag any specific language you need.

Proposed next steps:
- Legal: review the attached PDF + manifest sample in the bundle.
- Technical: if you want, we can run a quick joint session to walk through a pin and manifest (30 minutes).
- If you confirm acceptance of the attestation language we can issue a signed copy and provide a DocuSign link.

Attachments: Redwood_RFI_Answers_v1.pdf (includes manifest sample + policy excerpts)

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Product, Catalog & Governance
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Globex RFP: model catalog licensing + provenance questions

Mina / Karthik —

Looping ourselves in on Mina's response. A couple of internal notes for legal redline and QA before we hit DocuSign: 
- The '36 months retention' is fine but procurement sometimes pushes for 60 months. We should provide a contract addendum option and call out storage costs.
- For the manifest format: we should attach a checksum file and an example signed envelope (RFC examples). I'll draft a short appendix for the attestation clarifying the signing key rotation policy and key custody (KMS + HSM details).
- Notification windows: procurement often demands longer notice for license changes. Suggest we offer configurable notification windows per account (default timeline fine) and add explicit language about automatic fallback to pinned-compatible variants to reduce customer operational burden.

I'll prepare the attestation appendix and the key custody blurb for Mina's signature.

Neha
Senior Trust Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@globex.com>, Globex Legal <legal@globex.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Globex RFP: model catalog licensing + provenance questions — signed attestation and playbook

Alice / Globex Legal —

Thanks for the patience. Attached are the signed attestation and operational playbook we discussed:
- Model_Catalog_Attestation_Globex.pdf (signed) — contains an explicit statement of our catalog metadata practices, retention options, and lane for contract addenda.
- SBOM_summary.csv — condensed manifest example (columns: model_id, component, license, source_commit, artifact_sha256).
- pinning_playbook.md — step-by-step process for pin requests, rollout, rollback, and emergency backport handling.

Key clarifications made after internal review: 
- Retention: default 36 months, with a contract-addendum option for 60 months (costed).
- Key custody: manifests and signatures are protected with customer-configurable KMS integration; we can arrange HSM-backed signing under Private deployments.
- Timeline guarantees: security-critical backports for pinned models are SLA-covered for Dedicated/Private customers (72 hours); Hosted customers receive prioritized mitigation and an automatic compatible fallback policy while we remediate.
- Notification: configurable notification windows; we will set Globex to 45-day recommended action + 75-day required action in your account by default while legal confirms.

Next steps:
1) If the attestation language looks good, I will send the DocuSign envelope (link below).
2) Jordan is available next week for a 30-minute technical walkthrough of the manifest and pin token lifecycle.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/envelopes/XYZ-123-Globex

Thanks,
Mina
Head of Product, Catalog & Governance
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
